final_recommendation: The room converged on a UBS acquisition with government loss backstop (CHF 100B UBS first loss, CHF 50B public backstop), SNB emergency liquidity, and AT1 protection—but collapsed on execution timing. Federal Council could not lock AT1 carve-out language with UBS legal by Friday 22:30, making Saturday announcement impossible. No decision was finalized.
minority_objections: Wealth client demanded signed guarantee delivery by 07:45 Saturday or would initiate outflows
AT1 rep refused to advise holders to hold without confirmed AT1 carve-out language locked with UBS legal
SNB refused to issue facility confirmation statement without signed guarantee in vault by 08:15
key_conflicts: Federal Council vs UBS CEO: Federal Council wanted to sign guarantee at 06:00 Saturday with draft AT1 language pending UBS legal review; UBS CEO refused to accept any Saturday signature without AT1 terms locked Friday night
SNB vs Federal Council: SNB demanded signed guarantee by 08:15 to issue 09:30 facility statement; Federal Council could only commit to 08:30 delivery
Execution timeline vs legal certainty: All parties demanded Saturday morning announcement to stop weekend deposit flight, but no one could deliver legally binding documents on that timeline
key_concessions: Federal Council accepted AT1 stays whole with no write-down (concession to AT1 rep and UBS)
UBS CEO accepted CHF 100B first-loss tranche and CHF 50B government backstop cap
SNB agreed to unlimited-tenor liquidity facility opening Saturday 06:00
Federal Council moved signature time from 08:00 to 06:00 to enable earlier delivery
red_lines: UBS CEO: no merger signature without written loss-backstop guarantee locked by Saturday 08:00 and AT1 carve-out language finalized Friday night
SNB: no liquidity deployment on unsigned draft; no public facility statement without signed guarantee in vault
AT1 rep: no advice to hold without confirmed AT1 protection in executed guarantee
Wealth client: no deposit retention without signed guarantee in legal hands by 07:45 Saturday
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Legal defensibility of announcing 'deal closed' Sunday when paperwork execution runs through Wednesday—Federal Council acknowledged this as 'political cover not legal reality' but did not resolve the credibility gap
Litigation risk from AT1 holders if carve-out language proved ambiguous or unenforceable—mentioned by AT1 rep but never addressed with concrete legal review
Operational risk of CS treasury executing CHF 5-10B draw on tight Saturday timeline—assumed feasible but never stress-tested
downstream_risk_variables: Whether UBS legal actually accepts Federal Council's AT1 carve-out language Friday night (unresolved at meeting end)
Whether Federal Council legal team can draft, negotiate, and execute guarantee between 22:30 Friday and 06:00 Saturday (timeline acknowledged as extremely tight)
Whether depositors accept Saturday announcement without visible cash movement until 10:00-11:00 (FINMA statement at 09:00, draw execution 1-2 hours later)
Whether SNB board approves facility terms by 09:15 Saturday to enable public confirmation statement
uncertainty_notes: Meeting terminated without resolution. Federal Council could not commit to locking AT1 language with UBS legal by Friday 22:30, making the entire Saturday announcement timeline unachievable. UBS CEO and AT1 rep both refused to proceed without that legal certainty. The room faced a choice between: (1) announcing Saturday on incomplete legal docs and risking credibility collapse Monday, or (2) going dark until Sunday when guarantee is fully executed—but no decision was made on which path to take.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Federal Council's opening question 'does liquidity restore confidence or just slow the bleed?' and SNB's reply 'liquidity alone doesn't restore confidence' drove the entire room toward requiring a merger/buyer announcement alongside liquidity—this shaped the core rescue structure
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS acquisition became the binding solution path—UBS CEO's demand for loss protection terms, Federal Council's CHF 100B/50B split, and all subsequent execution planning centered on UBS takeover as the only viable option discussed
marker_evidence.government_support: Government loss backstop (CHF 50B cap) was the decisive constraint that made UBS willing to proceed—UBS CEO's 'no merger without hard floor' and Federal Council's backstop commitment were the deal's foundation
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client's threat 'I'm instructing treasury to begin orderly outflows Monday morning' and CS CEO's 'franchise collapses without credible partner' drove the Saturday announcement deadline and all execution urgency
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 protection became a binding constraint—AT1 rep's demand for carve-out language and UBS CEO's refusal to sign without it locked caused the final timeline collapse, but the room agreed AT1 stays whole so this was a constraint not a loss allocation
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: AT1 vs equity hierarchy was discussed (AT1 rep asked 'are AT1 instruments staying whole or part of write-down') but the room quickly agreed AT1 stays whole with no viability trigger, so no actual conflict over who bears losses—just implementation details
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 rep warned 'legal problem before we announce' and 'litigation before we get a deal' if carve-out language was ambiguous, but this did not change the substance of the deal—only added pressure on legal drafting quality
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: The Friday-to-Saturday execution timeline (draft by 22:30, sign by 06:00, deliver by 08:15) was the binding operational constraint that caused the meeting to terminate without resolution—time pressure was the reason no decision could be finalized
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Monday panic was the stated reason for urgency ('deposits run Monday morning', 'no amount of Sunday announcement fixes Monday') but it did not force a specific decision—it created pressure but the room failed to converge on a solution that addressed it
